requirements.original: int2bit(in integer invalue, in integer length) return bitstring
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2bit` has the signature `int2bit(in integer invalue, in integer length) return bitstring`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- int2bit(in integer invalue, in integer length) return bitstring

requirements.original: This function converts a single integer value to a single bitstring value.
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2bit` converts a single integer value into a single bitstring value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- This function converts a single integer value to a single bitstring value.

requirements.original: The resulting string is length bits long.
requirements.canonical: The bitstring returned by `int2bit` IS exactly `length` bits long.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- The resulting string is length bits long.

requirements.original: For the purposes of this conversion, a bitstring shall be interpreted as a positive base 2 integer value.
requirements.canonical: For the conversion performed by `int2bit`, a bitstring SHALL be interpreted as a positive base 2 integer value.

ambiguity.issue: The value 0 is a valid result/argument, so the bitstring is interpreted as a non-negative (not strictly positive) integer.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- For the purposes of this conversion, a bitstring shall be interpreted as a positive base 2 integer value.

requirements.original: The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2bit`, the rightmost bit IS the least significant bit.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.

requirements.original: The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2bit`, the leftmost bit IS the most significant bit.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- The rightmost bit is least significant, the leftmost bit is the most significant.

requirements.original: The bits 0 and 1 represent the decimal values 0 and 1 respectively.
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2bit`, the bits 0 and 1 represent the decimal values 0 and 1 respectively.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- The bits 0 and 1 represent the decimal values 0 and 1 respectively.

requirements.original: If the conversion yields a value with fewer bits than specified in the length parameter, then the bitstring shall be padded on the left with zeros.
requirements.canonical: If the conversion yields fewer bits than specified by the `length` parameter, `int2bit` SHALL pad the resulting bitstring on the left with zeros.
requirements.condition: the conversion yields fewer bits than length
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- If the conversion yields a value with fewer bits than specified in the length parameter, then the bitstring shall be padded on the left with zeros.

requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2bit`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more bits than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: If `invalue` is less than zero, the call of `int2bit` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more bits than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more bits than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:
requirements.canonical: If the conversion yields a return value with more bits than specified by `length`, the call of `int2bit` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the result needs more than length bits
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.3 -- invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more bits than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.original: int2enum ( in integer inpar, out Enumerated_type outpar)
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2enum` has the signature `int2enum(in integer inpar, out Enumerated_type outpar)` and has no return value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.4 -- int2enum ( in integer inpar, out Enumerated_type outpar)

requirements.original: This function converts an integer value into an enumerated value of a given enumerated type.
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2enum` converts an integer value into an enumerated value of a given enumerated type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.4 -- This function converts an integer value into an enumerated value of a given enumerated type.

requirements.original: The integer value shall be provided as in parameter and the result of the conversion shall be stored in an out parameter.
requirements.canonical: The integer value to be converted by `int2enum` SHALL be provided as the `in` parameter `inpar`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.4 -- The integer value shall be provided as in parameter and the result of the conversion shall be stored in an out parameter.

requirements.original: The integer value shall be provided as in parameter and the result of the conversion shall be stored in an out parameter.
requirements.canonical: The result of the conversion performed by `int2enum` SHALL be stored in the `out` parameter `outpar`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.4 -- The integer value shall be provided as in parameter and the result of the conversion shall be stored in an out parameter.

requirements.original: The type of the out parameter determines the type into which the in parameter is converted.
requirements.canonical: The type of the actual parameter passed to the `out` parameter `outpar` of `int2enum` determines the enumerated type into which `inpar` is converted.

improper_terms.proper: actual parameter passed to the out formal parameter

ambiguity.issue: The text says 'the type of the out parameter'; the formal parameter type is the generic Enumerated_type, so the type of the actual parameter is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.4 -- The type of the out parameter determines the type into which the in parameter is converted.

requirements.original: The type of the out parameter determines the type into which the in parameter is converted. int2enum ( in integer inpar, out Enumerated_type outpar)
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter passed to `outpar` of `int2enum` SHALL be a variable of an enumerated type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.4 -- The type of the out parameter determines the type into which the in parameter is converted. int2enum ( in integer inpar, out Enumerated_type outpar)

requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2enum`.

readings: If `inpar` does not equal the integer value associated with any enumerated value of the type of `outpar`, the call of `int2enum` SHALL cause an error (C.0, no explicit exception-handling rule).
If `inpar` does not equal the integer value associated with any enumerated value of the type of `outpar`, `int2enum` SHALL NOT cause an error and `outpar` remains unchanged or unbound.
ambiguity.issue: No error cause is listed for an integer that has no associated enumerated value; the canonical text only restates the general error causes. Reading 1 (error via C.0) is the most likely.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.4 -- The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.6 -- The rightmost hexadecimal digit is least significant, the leftmost hexadecimal digit is the most significant.

requirements.original: The number of hexadecimal digits provided shall be multiples of 2 since one octet is composed of two hexadecimal digits.
requirements.canonical: The octetstring produced by `int2oct` SHALL contain a number of hexadecimal digits that is a multiple of 2, since one octet is composed of two hexadecimal digits.

readings: The result of `int2oct` SHALL contain an even number of hexadecimal digits (i.e. a leading zero digit is added when the value has an odd number of significant digits).
Some user-provided hexadecimal digit sequence SHALL have an even length.
ambiguity.issue: 'The number of hexadecimal digits provided' does not say who provides the digits; int2oct takes no hexadecimal input, so the first reading (property of the result) was chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.1.6 -- The number of hexadecimal digits provided shall be multiples of 2 since one octet is composed of two hexadecimal digits.

requirements.condition: the conversion yields fewer digits than length octets

readings: If the result has fewer than 2*length hexadecimal digits, `int2oct` SHALL pad the octetstring on the left with zero digits up to `length` octets.
If the result has fewer than `length` hexadecimal digits, `int2oct` SHALL pad it on the left with zeros up to `length` hexadecimal digits.
ambiguity.issue: The sentence was copied from int2hex: it says 'hexstring' instead of 'octetstring' and compares hexadecimal digits with 'length', which counts octets (C.1.6-s003). Reading 1 was chosen because it is consistent with C.1.6-s003.
